top.headline: Democrats Sue Trump Administration Over Election-Interference Threats
top.blurb: Democratic groups sued the administration Tuesday, accusing it of using unfounded voter-fraud claims and threats of prosecution to pressure states on how they run elections. The suit names Trump, DOJ and DHS as defendants and cites a parallel DOJ push to block roughly 20,000 California mail ballots pending citizenship checks.

top.headline: Trump Leans Into Unprecedented Power Ahead of the Midterms
top.blurb: Less than two weeks before Election Day, NPR catalogs a Justice Department search of a congresswoman's home, tree removal in D.C. against a judge's order, and Russia dealings that defy congressional sanctions. A presidential historian calls Trump a 'unilateralist' using executive power against opponents, not just gridlock.

top.headline: White House Gives Politico 48 Hours to Retract Stories or Face 'Consequences'
top.blurb: White House Counsel Will Scharf demanded Politico retract three stories about chief of staff Susie Wiles, issue a public apology and scrub its archives, warning of an 'immediate review' of the outlet's White House relationship otherwise. Politico had not responded as of the deadline.

more.headline: Katie Zacharia Ousted as White House Press Secretary After Five Days
more.blurb: Trump was reportedly blindsided to learn his new press secretary had never passed the bar exam after introducing her as an attorney; officials called her debut briefing shaky.

top.headline: Election Commission Orders UP Voter-List Recheck as Congress Alleges 16,000 Irregularities
top.blurb: Uttar Pradesh's chief electoral officer ordered action against officials over errors in the special intensive revision of rolls in Pilibhit Sadar. Congress says more than 16,000 names were altered between July and September, amid continuing protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

more.headline: Bengaluru Blast: Worker Loses Two Fingers to Device Disguised as a Torch
more.blurb: A device disguised as a torch exploded at a construction site on October 20, injuring two workers; preliminary investigation suggests it may have been an improvised explosive device, though police have not officially confirmed that.

more.headline: Andhra Pradesh Pauses Local Body Polls After Supreme Court Order on YSRCP Plea
more.blurb: The state election commission paused publication of its final candidate list for urban local body polls after the Supreme Court directed a postponement on a YSRCP petition, with a further order expected shortly.

top.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Threatens US Bases Over Hormuz Tanker Routes
top.blurb: Iran's IRGC says its navy struck four ships involved in Gulf oil transfers and that three more hit mines near Hormuz, and has warned of widening the confrontation to US bases if Washington keeps backing tanker routes it calls illegal. Trump denies active negotiations with Tehran and says the standoff will resolve 'fairly soon.'

top.headline: Witkoff Pushes Putin to Restart Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks
top.blurb: US envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelensky in Norway, then flew to Moscow; Russia says Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated talks as soon as next month. Moscow has given no ground on controlling occupied Donetsk or blocking Ukraine's NATO ambitions, and a ceasefire still isn't a precondition.

top.headline: Qatar and France Call for Hormuz Reopening and Full Gaza Ceasefire Implementation
top.blurb: After meeting in Doha, Emir Tamim and Macron jointly called for restoring free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz 'without constraints or fees' and condemned Iranian attacks on regional states. They also urged unhindered aid into Gaza and opposed West Bank annexation.

more.headline: EU Unveils Revised Arctic Strategy as Russian and US Pressure Grows
more.blurb: The European Commission's new strategy puts security first, citing Russian drone incursions and GPS jamming, and backs a Greenland-to-Europe fibre cable partly to reduce reliance on US satellite links.

top.headline: HBO's 'Youth': Where Sharon Horgan's New Dramedy Lands in Her Canon
top.blurb: NPR's Pop Culture Happy Hour takes up Horgan's new HBO series, in which she plays Alex, a 50-year-old divorcee facing several personal and professional crossroads at once, and weighs where the show falls against her earlier, sharper work like 'Catastrophe' and 'Bad Sisters.'

bengal.headline: Kolkata Stampede: CM Suvendu Adhikari Asks Opposition Not to Politicise Tragedy
bengal.blurb: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari appealed to opposition parties not to politicise the Durga Puja pandal stampede that killed 19, as the Trinamool Congress pressed questions about the puja committee's leadership.

bengal.headline: TMC Attacks Bengal CM, Kolkata Police Over Pandal Stampede
bengal.blurb: Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress blamed the state's new BJP administration and Kolkata Police for failures that led to the fatal stampede, sharpening the first major opposition broadside since the party lost power.

bengal.headline: Durga Puja Bookstall Vandalism: Left Moves High Court as BJP, RSS Condemn Attacks
bengal.blurb: Left parties say their Durga Puja bookstalls were vandalised across the state and have petitioned the Calcutta High Court over one removal in Jadavpur; some BJP and RSS leaders have also condemned the attacks.

travel.headline: A Volcano-Carved Hideaway: Lonely Planet's Guide to Montserrat
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet named the quiet Caribbean island of Montserrat, known for its volcanic scenery and black-sand beaches, among its Best in Travel picks for 2027, calling it an under-visited hideaway.

travel.headline: Nepal's Newest National Parks Drive Tiger Recovery, But New Concerns Arise
travel.blurb: Nepal's tiger count has grown to 429, up from 355 in 2022, but the gains are concentrated in newer parks while Bardiya, an older reserve, saw numbers decline, raising new human-wildlife conflict and leopard-displacement concerns.

happy.headline: A Kansas Girl Ran Off to Join the Circus and Changed the Tattoo World
happy.blurb: Born Nora Stevens in Emporia, Kansas, Maud Stevens Wagner toured as a circus acrobat before becoming one of America's first known female tattoo artists, inking clients by hand at a time when women couldn't yet vote.

tech_top.headline: Meta Plans a New Class of Non-Voting Stock to Fund Its AI Buildout
tech_top.blurb: Meta will issue a non-voting Class C share as a dividend on every existing share, raising capital for AI spending without diluting Zuckerberg's or other holders' control. The filing cites tougher fundraising markets after huge recent raises by Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI.
tech_top.pm_note: Watch how your own company's AI spend gets financed — non-voting share classes let incumbents fund infrastructure at scale without ceding governance, a structure likely to spread.

tech_top.headline: While Amazon Blocks AI Agents, Walmart Rolls Out the Welcome Mat
tech_top.blurb: Walmart launched Agent Gateway, letting approved AI agents search inventory and buy on a shopper's behalf over the Model Context Protocol, with per-agent profiles and spending limits. It's a direct contrast with Amazon, which recently began blocking AI agents from completing purchases.
tech_top.pm_note: Two incumbents making opposite bets on agentic commerce is a live experiment — track which one converts browsing-agent traffic into revenue without cannibalizing margin.

tech_top.headline: Meta Says Muse Has Over 10 Million Users, With Shopping a Top Activity
tech_top.blurb: Meta disclosed that its AI assistant Muse has crossed 10 million users, with shopping among the most common tasks people hand it — a usage signal that lines up with the company's new push into agentic commerce.
tech_top.pm_note: A consumer AI assistant finding real traction in shopping, not just chat, is the adoption benchmark to compare your own product's AI feature usage against.

tech_more.headline: Someone Opened a CashApp Account In Her Name. She Faces Years in Prison.
tech_more.blurb: Amanda Smith is charged with computer fraud over a scam CashApp account opened in her name; the company refused to share any information about the account because she couldn't prove she owned it.

tech_more.headline: Florida Police Say Scammers Used AI to Clone a Sheriff's Voice
tech_more.blurb: Osceola County police say scammers cloned Sheriff Steve Moser's voice with AI and used it to leave a convincing voicemail for a resident, the latest case of voice-cloning fraud targeting local officials.

tech_101.text: A common language that lets an AI agent connect to a company's systems — like Walmart's store inventory — without a custom integration for every retailer. Think of it as a standard plug shape instead of a different adapter for every wall socket.

Shares that pay out like regular stock but carry no vote on company decisions. Issuing them lets a company raise money from investors without handing over any control — Meta's founder keeps the same say over the company either way.

science.headline: Scientists Find Hidden 'In-Between' Materials That Form While Chemicals Are Heated
science.blurb: University of Warwick researchers identified short-lived intermediate materials that appear only while chemical ingredients are being heated, before vanishing into the final product. One find was a previously unknown form of bismuth vanadate, a material of interest for solar-driven hydrogen production.

science.headline: Astronauts' Hearts Just Passed a Surprising Test for Mars
science.blurb: A study of 13 astronauts who spent roughly six months on the ISS found their hearts recovered after return and handled a simulation of Mars's lighter gravity well, though researchers caution the sample is small and the Mars conditions were simulated, not real.

science.headline: Scientists Reverse 60 Years of Aging in Human Cells
science.blurb: University of Bonn researchers reprogrammed blood cells drawn from an 80-year-old donor into neural stem cells that tested, by molecular markers, as under 20 years old — achieved by converting immature red blood cells rather than skin or other tissue.

philosophy.headline: Sometimes You 'Just Know' Something's Off — But How?
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Marc Moffett argues that a gut sense something is wrong — a creepy stranger, a phishing email — can justify belief much like perception does. The mind takes the content as actual, he argues, and that 'cognitive posture,' not a mere feeling, is what makes it a reason to act.

philosophy.headline: Does the Principle of Sufficient Reason Make Panpsychism True?
philosophy.blurb: Sam Kimpton-Nye examines whether the old rationalist demand that everything have an explanation — stated by Leibniz and Spinoza — pushes toward panpsychism, the view that mind is a basic feature of matter rather than something that emerges only in brains.

philosophy.headline: Why Real Intelligence Is Something More Than Optimisation
philosophy.blurb: Sasha Mudd warns that if intelligence is just optimisation, machines will outrun us by definition. Drawing on Kant against Hume's view of reason as a mere tool, she argues real intelligence is self-rule — the capacity to question one's own ends, not just pursue them efficiently.

philosophy_101.text: The idea, traced to Leibniz, that everything which exists or happens has a reason or cause — nothing is just a brute, unexplained fact. Critics, including Hume, questioned whether that's actually true of the universe.

A gut sense that something is true or false, arrived at without working through an argument. Philosophers debate whether that sense is just a feeling, or whether — like seeing a tree — it can genuinely justify a belief.
